title: Quality roles and links to the principles
blurb: Say who does what for quality, from senior user to project support, and how the quality practice supports each PRINCE2 principle.
question: How does the quality practice apply the 'tailor to suit the project' principle?

teach.h: Quality is shared across the roles
teach.body: No single role owns quality. Users say what they need and accept the result; suppliers build products to the required standard; the project manager plans and coordinates; teams carry out checks; support keeps the records; the board approves and assures; and the business provides independent quality assurance. In plain English: everyone has a quality job, and PRINCE2 writes down who does which part.

head: Role
Main quality contribution
rows: Approves the PPD and the QMA
Accountable for quality of supplier products
Prepares PPD, product descriptions and QMA
Builds to product descriptions; updates register
Assures the board quality controls are in place
Maintains the quality register and records

teach.body: The senior user represents the users and is accountable for capturing user requirements, so the users' quality expectations and acceptance criteria come through this role, and the product is accepted on the users' behalf. The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of the products delivered by suppliers and for their technical integrity, and commits supplier resources to quality work.

The project manager prepares the project product description, product descriptions for key products and the quality management approach, and makes sure team managers apply the agreed quality controls. In managing product delivery, the team manager updates the quality register and tells the project manager when quality activities are complete. Project support maintains the registers and quality records; it must stay separate from assurance.

steps.label: CS / MP
steps.sub: QMA in work packages; register updated

head: Principle
Quality link
rows: Quality activities fit the delivery approach and products
Quality specifications, methods and reviewers per product
Work traces to the justification; quality enables benefits
Quality checked and reported at each stage end
Past quality lessons shape the approach
Quality responsibilities set in the QMA

teach.h: Focus on products or manage by exception?

teach.body: Kestrel Valley Transport is building a live bus-times app in short iterations. Senior user Joanne Pike, head of customer services, supplies requirements and will accept the app for passengers. Senior supplier Arun Mehta, the agency's delivery director, answers for the agency's code quality. Project manager Ben Achterberg tailors quality: quick user trials each iteration instead of a heavy formal review cycle, as fits an iterative approach. Project support logs every trial in the quality register.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Naming quality reviewers in a product description applies FOCUS ON PRODUCTS, not manage by exception; tolerance is the manage by exception link. (2) The senior supplier, not the senior user, is accountable for the quality of supplier products. (3) Project support maintains the quality register but cannot do assurance.

items: Senior user: user requirements, expectations and acceptance on the users' behalf.
Senior supplier: accountable for quality of supplier products and technical integrity.
PM prepares PPD, product descriptions and QMA; board approves the PPD and QMA.
Team manager updates the quality register; project support maintains registers and records.
Tailor: only the quality activities that suit the delivery approach and products.
Focus on products: per-product specifications; manage by exception: quality tolerance.

summary: You can now say who does what for quality, from the business layer to project support. You can also explain how the quality practice supports the principles, especially tailoring, focus on products and manage by exception.

A.q: How does the quality practice apply the 'tailor to suit the project' principle?
options: By applying the same set of quality checks to every project
By asking the business layer to set each product's quality tolerance
By recording every quality activity in the project's daily log
By matching quality activities to the delivery approach and products
A.why: The quality practice tailors by requiring only those quality activities that are appropriate to the delivery approach and product characteristics (manual 8.7, tab 8.3).

whyNot.0: Identical checks on every project is the opposite of tailoring.
whyNot.1: Setting tolerances applies manage by exception, not tailoring, and each product's quality tolerance sits in its product description rather than being set by the business layer.
whyNot.2: Quality activities are recorded in the quality register.

A.q: Which role is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers?
A.why: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and for their technical integrity.

whyNot.0: The senior user represents users and specifies requirements and benefits.
whyNot.2: The executive owns the business case and is ultimately accountable for the project, not supplier product quality.
whyNot.3: The team manager produces products but is not accountable on the board for supplier quality.

A.q: Which role maintains the quality register and quality records?
A.why: Project support maintains registers, including the quality register, and quality records, under the project manager.

whyNot.0: Project assurance reviews the register for the board; it does not maintain it.
whyNot.1: The executive directs the project and does not administer registers.
whyNot.3: Quality assurance is independent of the project management team.

B.q: A project manager records the named quality reviewers and approvers in each product description. Which principle is mainly being applied?
B.why: Product descriptions define each product's purpose, composition, derivation, format, quality criteria and method; documenting reviewers there applies focus on products.

whyNot.0: Manage by exception sets tolerances to delegate authority, which naming reviewers does not do.
whyNot.2: Manage by stages concerns stage-by-stage planning and decisions.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience concerns seeking and using lessons.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. The project board approves the project product description and the QMA.
2. Project support may carry out project assurance on quality.
3. The senior user is accountable for capturing user requirements.
4. The senior supplier accepts the project product on behalf of the users.
B.why: In directing a project the board approves the PPD and the QMA (1), and the senior user is accountable for capturing user requirements (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: project support must be kept separate from assurance.
whyNot.1: Both are false: support cannot do assurance, and acceptance is by the board on behalf of the users.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the board accepts on the users' behalf, with the senior user representing users.

B.q: A product's quality is forecast to fall outside its agreed quality tolerance. Which principle does escalating this apply?
B.why: Quality tolerance sets the permissible deviation before escalation; escalating a forecast breach applies manage by exception.

whyNot.1: Focus on products defines the product and its specifications, not the escalation of deviations.
whyNot.2: Tailoring adapts the method to the project.
whyNot.3: Manage by stages is about planning and deciding stage by stage.

C.q: Which role prepares the product descriptions, and in which process does the board approve the quality management approach?
options: Senior user; starting up a project
C.why: The project manager prepares product descriptions for key products, and the board approves the QMA in directing a project.

whyNot.0: The senior user supplies requirements; the QMA does not exist yet in starting up.
whyNot.1: Team managers contribute and build to product descriptions; the board is not involved in managing product delivery.
whyNot.3: Project support assists with administration; approval is a board decision in directing a project.

C.q: How does the quality practice support 'ensure continued business justification'?
options: By tracing work to products linked to the justification
By setting the business case tolerance for benefits
By asking quality assurance to approve the business case
By replacing the business case with acceptance criteria
C.why: Product-based quality avoids spending resources on work that cannot be traced back to the business justification, and quality products enable the benefits.

whyNot.1: Benefits tolerance sits in the benefits management approach, not the quality practice.
whyNot.2: The business case is approved by the board and owned by the executive.
whyNot.3: Acceptance criteria support the business case; they do not replace it.

C.q: In managing product delivery, which role updates the quality register, and which principle does checking the register at each stage end support?
C.why: The team manager updates the quality register when executing a work package; checking it at each stage boundary to feed the end stage report supports manage by stages.

whyNot.0: Managing product delivery is the team manager's process, and the stage-end check links to stages.
whyNot.2: Project assurance reviews the register; it does not update it in managing product delivery.
whyNot.3: The senior supplier sits on the board and does not update the register.

reteach.title: Building a garden room
reteach.question: Who looks after quality when you have a garden room built?

blocks.body: You (the user) say what the room must be and sign it off. The builder's director answers for the quality of the build. The project manager writes the plan and specs. The site foreman builds to spec and logs every check. The office assistant keeps the paperwork. A building control officer from outside checks the inspections are good enough. A simple shed project would not need every formal check: that is tailoring.

blocks.text: The office assistant files the inspection results but must not be the one assuring the project.

explain.body: Represents users, is accountable for capturing user requirements, and the product is accepted on the users' behalf.

test.q: Which role is accountable for capturing user requirements?
test.why: The senior user represents the users and is accountable for capturing user requirements.

whyNot.0: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of supplier products.
whyNot.1: The PM documents requirements but the senior user is accountable for them.
whyNot.3: The business layer commissions the project and provides quality assurance.

explain.body: Accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and their technical integrity.

test.q: For what is the senior supplier accountable?
test.why: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and their technical integrity.

whyNot.1: Benefits are specified and realized by the senior user.

explain.body: Require only those quality activities that suit the delivery approach and the product characteristics.

test.q: Which principle is applied when quality activities are matched to the delivery approach and product characteristics?
test.why: The quality practice applies tailoring by requiring only those quality activities that are appropriate to the delivery approach and product characteristics.

whyNot.0: Manage by stages is about stage-by-stage planning and decisions.
whyNot.1: Learn from experience is about seeking and applying lessons.
whyNot.2: Focus on products defines products and their quality, not how much quality activity suits the project.

explain.body: Quality tolerance is the allowed deviation before escalation: the manage by exception link.

test.q: Which quality concept links most directly to manage by exception?
test.why: Quality tolerance is the permissible deviation before escalation, which applies manage by exception.

whyNot.0: Product descriptions apply focus on products.
whyNot.2: The quality register records quality activities and results.
whyNot.3: Acceptance methods describe how acceptance will be confirmed.
